subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host `openclaw models auth login` fail closed before provider auth starts, or should OpenClaw design authenticated gateway-side credential forwarding for this flow?
rationale: The source-level fix shape is clear, but the permanent behavior decides whether a node host may acquire and transfer gateway-owned OAuth material, which is a product/security boundary automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Fail closed before auth starts
options.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable instruction to run auth on the gateway host, while preserving loopback/tunnel setups.

options.title: Forward credentials to the gateway
options.body: Design a credential-transfer RPC or setup flow that writes directly to the gateway-owned auth store without leaving node-local OAuth material behind.

options.title: Warn but allow local writes
options.body: Keep the current permissive behavior with a warning, accepting that users can still consume OAuth credentials into the wrong store.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth starts
recommendation.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable instruction to run auth on the gateway host, while preserving loopback/tunnel setups.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc already authored the maintainer-side guard attempt for the exact credential-boundary behavior and recently touched the auth command surface.
